subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Ductus Venosus, Biophysical Profile, NST and CTG

steps.tx: Flow reversal during atrial contraction in the fetal venous shunt, the **ductus venosus a-wave**, signals failing cardiac compensation. In early growth restriction it is the strongest Doppler predictor of stillbirth. Absent or reversed a-wave at viable gestation usually triggers delivery. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: A reversed ductus venosus a-wave signals failing compensation and usually triggers delivery.

steps.tx: The five component ultrasound and heart rate assessment scoring fetal wellbeing is the **biophysical profile**. Breathing, movement, tone, fluid and heart reactivity each score two points. Scores of eight to ten reassure, zero to four demand delivery. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: The biophysical profile scores five components, with eight to ten reassuring.

steps.tx: Recording fetal heart accelerations with movement without contractions is the **non-stress test**. Two accelerations in twenty minutes make it reactive and reassuring. It is the antenatal test of choice for most high risk surveillance. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: The non-stress test seeks two accelerations in twenty minutes for reassurance.

steps.tx: Continuous electronic recording of fetal heart and contractions is **cardiotocography**. Baseline, variability, accelerations and decelerations are read systematically. Interpretation frameworks classify traces as reassuring, non reassuring or abnormal. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Cardiotocography records heart and contractions read systematically by four features.

vis.caption: Baseline rate. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Beat to beat fluctuation of the baseline between five and twenty five beats is **baseline variability**. It is the single most reassuring CTG feature when normal. Reduced variability with decelerations is the most ominous combination. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Baseline variability is the most reassuring CTG feature when normal.

steps.tx: The systematic reading mnemonic covering contractions, baseline, variability, accelerations, decelerations and overall impression is taught as **DR C BRAVADO**. It prevents missed features in a pressured labour ward. Documentation follows the same sequence every time. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: DR C BRAVADO systematises CTG reading so no feature is missed.

steps.tx: A reactive trace needs accelerations, whose absence alone is not pathological in a sleeping fetus, termed the **sleep cycle caveat**. Fetal sleep lasts up to forty minutes with quiet variability. Extending monitoring usually captures wakefulness. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Absent accelerations may reflect fetal sleep lasting forty minutes, so monitoring extends.

steps.tx: Combining Doppler and biophysical testing in early growth restriction follows **integrated surveillance**. Umbilical changes come first, then cerebral, then venous, then biophysical deterioration. This sequence times delivery to the last safe moment. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Integrated surveillance follows the Doppler to biophysical deterioration sequence for timing.

steps.tx: Antenatal CTG has high false positive rates, so abnormal traces prompt **confirmatory assessment**. Reviewing the whole clinical picture, scalp stimulation or blood sampling refines decisions. Unnecessary caesareans follow blind trace reaction. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Abnormal antenatal traces need confirmatory assessment because false positives are common.
